I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou's soils — silty loam, decent organic matter if I've managed it right. The wheat-maize rotation is what everyone here does, and I've refined my inputs over time. With only 6 mu and three mouths to feed, I can't afford to waste money on excess fertilizer, but I also can't afford a poor harvest.

**My thinking crop by crop:**

**Winter wheat (October–June, full 6 mu):** I'll plant an improved high-yielding variety — something like Jimai 22 or Shimai 15, which do well in Hebei conditions. After 30 years I know the base fertilizer goes in before planting, with a topdress at jointing stage. I'll do 14 kg N/mu total — I've seen what over-fertilizing does to lodging and to the water table. The China Agricultural University station right here in Quzhou has been pushing water-saving irrigation for decades, and I've listened. Three irrigations: the winter water (yueban shui) to protect roots, the jointing water, and the heading water. That's enough. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in autumn, then aphid and rust control in spring.

**Summer maize (June–September, full 6 mu after wheat harvest):** I go straight in with no-till direct seeding right after the combine harvests wheat. No time to waste — every day matters for getting maize established before the heat peaks. I use a hybrid like Xianyu 335 or Zhengdan 958. Summer is rainy season here so I only plan for two supplemental irrigations unless it's a drought year. Nitrogen goes in at planting and again at the big bell stage — 16 kg/mu total. Two pesticide applications: pre-emergence herbicide and one pass for corn borer in mid-summer.
